summary: A two-part look at genocide's ancient roots, from a prehistoric massacre in Kenya to Rome's annihilation of Carthage in 146 BCE, urged on by Cato the Elder, and how perpetrators are motivated, from Mithridates to Rwanda.

evidence.note: Nataruk mass grave at Lake Turkana dated to roughly 8000 BCE
Yamnaya / Corded Ware replacement of Globular Amphora people, c. 3000 BCE
long Cato the Elder segment begins: career, Iberia, misogyny, figs speech
extended discussion of Roman slavery after Cato's mass enslavement in Iberia
Cato's senatorial mission to Carthage and his campaign for its destruction
Third Punic War, fall of Carthage in 146 BCE, massacre and enslavement of survivors
Mithridates orders the massacre of Romans and Italians in Asia, 88 BCE
Aryanization and Holocaust perpetrators discussed as a case of genocide for gain
RTLM radio and the limits of propaganda as a cause of the Rwandan genocide
1994 Rwandan genocide segment sets the latest covered year

notes: Thematic survey, not one subject. Primary set to the Third Punic War per title; Cato could arguably be co-primary (long segment). Covered span should start at Nataruk (~8000 BCE) but schema floor is -5000, so clamped. It ends at Rwanda 1994; Nataruk and Rwanda are secondary subjects with real airtime; the 2022 US anti-trans rhetoric is framing, not story. Yamnaya segment dropped from subjects due to the 5-subject cap. No theme for 'theory of genocide/perpetrator psychology'.
